title: Emplacement of the Bushveld Complex
summary: The Bushveld Complex of South Africa, described as the world's largest layered igneous intrusion and host to chromium, platinum-group and vanadium deposits, was emplaced about 2,060 to 2,055 million years ago. High-precision zircon dating puts its Rustenburg Layered Suite at about 2056.3 to 2055.5 million years ago, built up over at least 0.6 million years.

uncertainty.note: Years are Ma with no 1950 offset. Range is the 2060-2055 Ma interval for the whole complex (Scoates et al. 2021); the Rustenburg Layered Suite dates 2056.28 +/- 0.15 to 2055.54 +/- 0.27 Ma (Mungall et al. 2016).

as_recorded.value: ages range from 2056.28±0.15 Myr for the UG1 to 2055.54±0.27 Myr for the Merensky Reef
built incrementally over an ∼5 Myr interval from 2060 to 2055 Ma with a peak in magma flux at c. 2055–2056 Ma

where.modern_name: Bushveld Igneous Complex, South Africa (Wikidata point; the layered suite spans about 450 km east-west and 350 km north-south)
where.historical_name: Kaapvaal Craton, southern Africa; no polities

importance.justification: World's largest layered intrusion and a major source of chromium and platinum-group metals.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the single pin: the complex is five lobes across hundreds of km, so the Wikidata point is a rough centre. No paleo-position: 2,056 Ma lies outside the plate models. Years carry no 1950 offset.
